newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas supported by extended cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas supported by extended cold.

text.p: U.S spot natgas prices held mostly steady Tuesday, with some minor gains evident in the Gulf market due to the well below-normal temperatures in Texas and Louisiana, market sources said.
Gulf Coast prices were up about five cents to the $3.97-4.02 per mmBtu range as temperatures in the 20s and 30s degrees Fahrenheit continued to drain supplies in Texas.
However, with storage inventories in the area at fairly substantial levels, large volumes of gas were likely being withdrawn to meet heating demand, sources said.
Further east, where storage levels were about 20 percent ahead of year-ago, New York city-gate prices fell by about 35 cents to about $4.25.
Sources attributed the softening to active storage withdrawals and slightly milder weather forecast for the Northeast Wednesday.
However, another cold front is forecast to arrive Thursday, pushing temperatures to much-below-normal levels through next week.

In the Midcontinent, where buyers are experiencing a brief respite from the frigid temperatures, prices drifted a few cents lower to the $4.25-4.30 range. On NGPL, prices were at a discount in the $4.00-4.10 area.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the $4.10-4.40 range.
Cold, arctic air is expected to return late Thursday throughout most of the Midwest and continue through at least early next week, dragging temperatures as much as 30 degrees below normal.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were mostly steady in the $4.18-4.23 range, with deals reported done anywhere from $4.05 to $4.27.
At the southern California border, prices were similarly stable around $4.30 as below-normal temperatures continued to attract buyers to the marketplace.

Also, storage levels are still lagging behind year-ago levels in the Consuming Region West, making it difficult for buyers to rely on inventories. As of January 3, AGA reported that stocks in the West were 58 percent full, still 74 bcf behind year-ago.
